`add_route_arg` sets `arg_name = match.groups()[0]` and checks `if arg_name in args` before inserting `args[arg_name] = type_`. So at each evaluation, `len(args)` is the number of previously seen dynamic argument names in that route, while `len(arg_name)` is the character length of the current name. The suite includes counterexamples: for `/a/[longname]/[x]`, when processing `[x]`, `len(arg_name) = 1` and `len(args) = 1`, so `1 > 1` is false; similarly later routes have short names like `q` or `c` after multiple prior args, which also make the relation false. Therefore the relationship does not hold for every evaluation.

## Answer
{"invariant_exists":false}

In `get_route_args`, the closure `args` starts as `{}` and grows by one entry each time `add_route_arg` finishes, because after the membership test it does `args[arg_name] = type_`. Inside `add_route_arg`, `arg_name` is just the matched route parameter name string. So the questioned relation compares the character length of the current parameter name against the count of previously collected parameter names.

That cannot be invariant over the suite. For example, in `/a/[longname]/[x]`, when `add_route_arg` is called for `[x]`, `args` already contains one prior entry (`longname`), so `len(args) == 1`, while `arg_name == "x"` so `len(arg_name) == 1`; thus `len(arg_name) > len(args)` is false. Since one evaluation already breaks it, the property is not an invariant.

## Answer
{"invariant_exists":false}
